title: House Robber II
description:
Houses are positioned around a ring. At index i, nums[i] gives the amount available there. Choose a set of houses with the largest possible total, subject to never selecting two neighboring houses. In this arrangement the first and last houses are neighbors as well as consecutive indices in the array. Return the maximum amount, not the chosen indices.

Any valid choice must leave out either the first house or the last house (possibly both). That lets you compare the best nonadjacent total for the line excluding the first house with the line excluding the last. Along either line, the best prefix comes from skipping its last house or taking that house after skipping the preceding one. Do not simply run the straight-street calculation over the whole ring, because it can select both endpoints illegally.

There is no obligation to select a house: an empty ring yields zero. A ring of one house has no other house to conflict with and returns that amount. For two houses, choose at most one. Values are nonnegative. In particular, a ring with values 2, 3, 2 has optimum three, rather than four from the two endpoint houses.

Example 1:

Input: nums = [2,3,2]
Output: 3

Example 2:

Input: nums = [1,2,3,1]
Output: 3

Example 3:

Input: nums = [5]
Output: 5

Constraints:

  • 0 <= nums.length <= 100
  • 0 <= nums[i] <= 10,000
  • For length greater than one, nums[0] and nums[-1] are adjacent.
